newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CAM files suit against Toho Oil purchase.
newsitem.headline: CAM files suit against Toho Oil purchase.

text.p: CAM International Holdings (CIHL) said on Monday it has filed a suit against three people and Toho Oil International Pte Ltd connected with the purported purchase of Toho Oil engine additive.

It said in a statement it was suing Raymond Chew, former executive chairman and managing director of CAM International Trading & Investments (CIS), former chief financial officer Ng Chee Tiong, and Lim Teong Kuan, also known as William Lim.
The company was claiming Singapore $3.57 million from the defendants, the statement said.
It said the company had obtained an injuction that froze each of the defendants' assets in Singapore up to the value of S$3.57 million, pending trial of the suit.
CAM also said See Choor Sen, Lau Chew Kwan, and William Lim have sued CIHL and its CIS subsidiary, Cheong Khee San & Co.
The suits seek a declaration that the purchase by CIS of Sino-Friendship Pte Ltd (SFS) for S$2.11 million was a sham and the registered shareholders of SFS were See and Lau.
Singapore's Criminal Affairs Department charged Raymond Chew with criminal breach of trust and forgery in May and June.
An ex-auditor, Cheong Khee San, was charged with abetment of forgery.
CIHL was suspended from trade on the Stock Exchange of Singapore after auditors reported suspicion of fraud to the Ministry of Finance on April 29 .
